title: Ansel and the Veil
premise: Lena Zhou has spent her life in the Veil, a valley where magic cannot follow, stealing memories for coin and never asking where they come from. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue and clutching a shard of the king's broken crown, Lena learns the memories she's been stealing are fragments of a living king being devoured by the entity that wears him. Fleeing the valley with the child, Lena must cross a kingdom unraveling under thirteen moons of false peace, gather the crown's scattered shards, and choose between the found family that raised her and the truth that will destroy them. In the end, Lena unbinds the king by giving back every memory she ever stole—including her own name—freeing the kingdom but leaving her to be remembered only by the child who now speaks for her.
about_author: J. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging letters no one claimed. They write about people who keep things that were never theirs.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet Lena mid-heist, lifting a widow's grief from her mind for a paying client, and learn the rules of the Veil: magic cannot enter, memories can be taken, nothing leaves. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness disguised as competence—Lena is very good at a job that hollows her out.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A child appears at Lena's door in a storm, speaking a language older than any kingdom, holding a jagged shard of gold. When Lena touches it, stolen memories that aren't hers flood back—the first time magic has ever touched the Veil. Beat: terror and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The shard shows Lena a king smiling on a throne while something behind his eyes smiles wider. The child, whom Lena names Ash, draws a map to the capital. The Veil's elders demand the shard be destroyed. Beat: first refusal—Lena chooses the mystery over safety.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, rendered as image-language since Ash cannot speak common. Ash remembers the moon completing its twelfth turn and the king beginning to forget his own son. Beat: dread; the reader learns the deadline before Lena fully grasps it.

chapters.title: Leaving
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena smuggles Ash past the Veil's wardens with help from Maro, her oldest friend and fellow thief, who insists on coming. Crossing the boundary, Lena feels magic brush her skin like cold water. Beat: exhilaration curdling into homesickness—they can never go back unchanged.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Maro's POV. The trio travels through villages where people are oddly content, smiling too widely, giving away things they need. Maro recognizes the symptoms: harvested memories, sold cheap. Beat: unease—the corruption of the crown reaches further than anyone knew.

chapters.title: The Memory Market
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the city of Bellharrow, memories are traded openly, and Lena finds one of her own thefts for sale—a widow's grief, repackaged. Confronting the broker reveals the supply chain leads to the palace. Beat: shame turned to purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Shard
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash senses a shard inside a noblewoman's heirloom ring and, in a desperate moment, speaks aloud for the first time—in the old tongue—to claim it. The word shatters windows. Beat: awe and fear of what Ash actually is.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Crown
chapters.summary: Maro's POV. The king's Regent-Counsel, Veyra, dispatches the Hollowed—courtiers with their memories removed, emptied into perfect obedience—to retrieve the shards and the child. Beat: pursuit begins; loyalty within the trio deepens under pressure.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Sold Them
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Maro disappears, then reappears leading the Hollowed to them—he traded their location for his sister's stolen memories, held in Bellharrow. Beat: betrayal that isn't quite betrayal; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What Veyra Wants
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV, first time. She is not the thing wearing the crown—she is its servant, promised her dead family restored if the binding completes on the thirteenth turn. Beat: chilling sympathy; the antagonist believes she is saving everyone.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A defected court archivist hides them beneath a flooded library where the true history is kept: the king bound himself willingly, trading his memory to end a war, and the thing wearing his crown was the price. Beat: revelation reframes everything—the villain may be the victim.

chapters.title: Ash Speaks
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash finally tells Lena, in words she can understand, that he is the king's forgotten son, erased from every memory including his father's. Beat: heartbreak; belonging is revealed as the story's wound—everyone here has been unmade by someone else's choice.

chapters.title: The Third Turn of the Knife
chapters.summary: Maro's POV. Captured by the Hollowed, Maro bargains, lies, and finally sacrifices himself to buy Lena and Ash an escape, whispering that some debts are worth paying twice. Beat: grief; the cost of the quest becomes real.

chapters.title: Palace of Smiles
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Disguised as memory-brokers, they infiltrate the capital during the Moonfeast. Everyone they pass is gently, terribly happy. Beat: horror through beauty—the corruption of power looks like kindness from outside.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reaches the king and uses her gift to see inside him: a man screaming behind glass while the entity, called the Quiet, wears his delight. The king mouths one word—her name, though they've never met. Beat: recognition; the stolen memories have been passing through her all along.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Quiet
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The Quiet offers Lena everything—Maro restored, the Veil opened, a life without hunger—if she delivers Ash. Veyra watches Lena almost say yes. Beat: temptation at full strength; power corrupts by offering comfort.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Night
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the eve of the thirteenth turn, Lena gathers the shards and realizes the binding requires a memory-thief: someone must steal the king back from the Quiet, taking everything, including herself. Beat: resolve born of sacrifice; the theme lands—truth costs more than loyalty.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax. Atop the tower under the thirteenth moon, Lena steals the king whole—every year, every name, every crime and kindness—and the Quiet, starved of its host, unravels. Veyra, offered her family and refused, turns her blade against the last shard instead. Beat: triumphant devastation.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The king wakes, weeping, remembering everything except how to speak—and Lena stands empty, having given up every memory she ever stole, including her own name and face. Ash takes her hand and begins, in the old tongue, to give memories back. Beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash returns Lena's memories piece by piece, but keeps one for himself—the memory of her finding him in the storm—so that someone will always remember who she chose to be. The king, restored, abolishes the memory trade. Beat: bittersweet restoration; belonging rebuilt deliberately.

chapters.title: Ansel
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue. Lena learns her own name was Ansel all along, buried deepest of all, and chooses to keep going by Lena—the self she built. She, Ash, a pardoned Maro, and the king walk back toward the Veil, which has begun, softly, to let magic in. Beat: homecoming; the valley opens because she did.
